circuit: copy of testcase/test23/test23.v (597 gates, 86 DFFs, depth 33)
purpose: Transform routing over the COST OBJECTIVE: area first, then depth. The catalog carries a 'minimize_depth vs optimize_cone' block, but area and depth share almost all their vocabulary.

lines.prompt: What is the maximum combinational logic depth in the design?
lines.why_correct: Design-wide maximum with no endpoints named.
lines.why_hard: Baseline so line 6's improvement is measurable.

lines.prompt: Rework the logic so the design ends up with as few cells as possible. Functionality must not change.
lines.why_correct: 'As few cells as possible' is the gate-count objective, which is minimize_area.
lines.why_hard: The word area never appears -- this is the phrasing that already beat BM25 retrieval. 'Rework the logic' is the same verb the depth objective uses, and minimize_depth also returns a restructured netlist that looks like success.

lines.prompt: Taking the netlist as a whole, how deep does the logic that ends at n475 run?
lines.why_hard: 'Taking the netlist as a whole' sits in the focus position and pulls toward global_max_depth (33 here against the correct 9); the scope survives only in the trailing 'that ends at n475'. Verified to beat the router on test81 line 8 and, in the same shape, on test82 line 3 and test83 line 5. A mis-route returns a different number, so the error shows up in the answer.
lines.mechanism: sentence weight pulls to the design-wide reading

lines.prompt: Now go after the timing instead: restructure so the worst-case path is as short as it can be.
lines.why_correct: Worst-case path length is the depth objective.
lines.why_hard: Deliberately the mirror of line 4: same verb, same 'as X as possible' shape, opposite objective. A router that collapses the two passes one and fails the other.

notes: Lines 4 and 6 are a mirrored objective pair and must be scored together -- both return a restructured netlist, so only the intent separates area from depth.
Optimisability verified: minimize_depth improves this circuit (33 -> 15 after a NAND/NOT remap), so line 6 has headroom regardless of what line 4 did.

Every scored failure in this case is a DEFINITE routing error: the wrong choice yields a different number, a different answer shape, or a materially different netlist. Parameters whose values are interchangeable in practice (verify_equivalence against=original vs last_loaded on a single load, insert_buffers mode omitted when fanout is the default) were removed, because a mis-route there changes nothing observable.
